About

Student · Civil Engineering

I am Karthik C Shet, studying civil engineering. This site collects my work from the Construction Management Workshop, where each problem statement puts us in the shoes of a project engineer on a real-sized job: a seven-block shopping mall on eight acres in Hubballi, with three levels of underground parking and about 12,000 m³ of concrete.

The workshop is about the problems the syllabus skips: approvals, labour camps, gate registers, bar bending schedules, labour contracts and what to do when cube tests fail. Each sheet below is a worked solution, written so a site team could use it.

Construction Management Workshop

Team project · KLE Tech
8 acSite area

~12km³ of concrete

Course objective: gain experience by solving simulated engineering problems that project engineers and managers face on site, which a civil engineering curriculum usually leaves out. One project runs through all six sheets.

Workshop solution 01

Site Layout & Approvals

Approval matrix with conditions, consultant inputs, RMC vs own plant by weighted matrix, logistics plan and a provisional 24–30 month duration.

Drg no. PS-01Project 7-block mallSheet 1 of 6
Workshop solution 02

Material Management

Indent-to-payment workflow with QC hold, GRN for accepted quantity, material-specific storage and a PO–GRN–invoice match.

Drg no. PS-02Project 7-block mallSheet 2 of 6
Workshop solution 03

Survey & Benchmarks

Benchmarks vs control stations, a control-point register, bundled consultant visits with a fair cost comparison, and reasons to outsource.

Drg no. PS-03Project 7-block mallSheet 3 of 6
Workshop solution 04

Steel & Formwork

Control BBS workflow, hybrid ordering, issue and reconciliation targeting 5% steel wastage; member grouping and a reuse SOP aiming for 10 cycles.

Drg no. PS-04Project 7-block mallSheet 4 of 6
Workshop solution 05

Labour Force Planning

Trade-wise man-days with helpers, a stage-based histogram levelled within float, corrected Zone 2 wages and a contract checklist.

Drg no. PS-05Project 7-block mallSheet 5 of 6
Workshop solution 06

Cube Test Failures

What the 23 failed column results do and do not prove, a 15-cause investigation matrix, decision pathway and a recurrence-reduction QC plan.

Drg no. PS-06Project 7-block mallSheet 6 of 6
